author: Robert Carr
description: Browned turkey and lentils in a spiced tomato braise, served with deeply roasted cabbage and cold lemon-herb yogurt. Tomato paste, ginger and warm spices build flavor without a stock cube or salty bottled sauce.
equipment: Four shallow meal-prep containers and four sauce cups

groceryIngredients.note: 3.75 g total; use a fine salt weighing about 6 g per teaspoon.
About 9 g for the braise and 4 g for the yogurt.
Use a mild blend; see the measured lower-heat variation.
15 oz each; cooked, drained and rinsed, approximately 500 g drained total. Do not substitute dry lentils directly.
Need 2 tablespoons juice and 1 teaspoon zest.

ingredients: Cabbage: 1 lb (454 g) green cabbage, cut into 1-inch-wide ribbons
Cabbage: 2 teaspoons extra-virgin olive oil, 1/8 teaspoon (0.75 g) fine sea salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
Braise: 1 1/4 lb (567 g) plain 93% lean ground turkey
Braise: 1 large yellow onion (225 g peeled), finely diced
Braise: 3 garlic cloves (9 g peeled), minced, and 1 tablespoon (12 g) finely grated fresh ginger
Braise: 1 tablespoon salt-free mild berbere, 1 tablespoon sweet paprika, 1 teaspoon ground cumin and 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon
Braise: 2 tablespoons (32 g) no-salt-added tomato paste
Braise: one 28-oz (794 g) can no-salt-added crushed tomatoes
Braise: two 15-oz cans no-salt-added cooked lentils, drained and rinsed, approximately 500 g drained total
Braise: 1/2 cup (120 mL) water and 1/2 teaspoon (3 g) fine sea salt
Braise finish: 8 oz (227 g) baby spinach
Yogurt: 228 g plain 2% Greek yogurt, measured by weight
Yogurt: 2 tablespoons (30 g) fresh lemon juice and 1 teaspoon (2 g) finely grated lemon zest
Yogurt: 1 garlic clove (4 g peeled), finely grated
Yogurt: 1/2 cup (16 g) finely chopped fresh cilantro
instructions: Roast the cabbage: Heat the oven to 450 F. Toss 1 lb (454 g) cabbage ribbons with 2 teaspoons olive oil, 1/8 teaspoon (0.75 g) fine sea salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper on the sheet pan. Spread into a single layer. Once the oven is hot, roast for 20-25 minutes, turning at about 12 minutes, until tender with dark golden edges rather than blackened leaves.

Brown the turkey while the cabbage roasts: Heat 2 teaspoons olive oil in a 5-6-quart Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add 1 1/4 lb (567 g) ground turkey in a broad layer. Leave it undisturbed for 3 minutes, then turn and break into coarse crumbles. Cook for another 3-4 minutes so browned patches develop; avoid constantly stirring the meat into a fine, steamed crumble.

Build the braise: Add 225 g diced yellow onion to the turkey and cook for 5 minutes, stirring. Add 9 g minced garlic, 1 tablespoon (12 g) grated ginger, 1 tablespoon mild salt-free berbere, 1 tablespoon sweet paprika, 1 teaspoon cumin and 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon; stir for 30 seconds. Add 2 tablespoons (32 g) tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring until the paste darkens slightly without scorching.

Simmer: Stir in one 28-oz (794 g) can crushed tomatoes, the drained lentils from two 15-oz cans (about 500 g drained), 1/2 cup (120 mL) water and 1/2 teaspoon (3 g) fine sea salt. Scrape up the browned bits. Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick but still spoonable.

Make the cold yogurt during the simmer: Mix 228 g plain 2% Greek yogurt, 2 tablespoons (30 g) lemon juice, 1 teaspoon (2 g) lemon zest, 4 g grated garlic and 1/2 cup (16 g) chopped cilantro. The measured ingredients make about 280 g sauce. Refrigerate until portioning.

Finish and check doneness: Fold 8 oz (227 g) baby spinach into the braise in two additions of 4 oz (113-114 g) each. Cook for 2-3 minutes until wilted. Check that the turkey crumbles and the surrounding braise reach at least 165 F.

Portion: Weigh the cooked braise and portion evenly among four shallow containers. Weigh the cooked cabbage and distribute evenly among the same four meals. Pack about 70 g lemon-herb yogurt in each separate sauce cup. Keep the yogurt cold and add it only after reheating a meal. Refrigerate promptly rather than waiting for a deep pot of braise to cool on the counter.
notes: Timing: Allow about 55 minutes including chopping, preheating, browning and portioning. The cabbage, braise and yogurt are prepared in parallel. Use already-cooked canned lentils, not dry lentils; the stated time does not include cooking lentils from dry.

Heat control: Berbere varies enormously. For a hot blend, replace the 1 tablespoon berbere with 1 teaspoon berbere plus 2 teaspoons additional sweet paprika. This is in addition to the listed 1 tablespoon sweet paprika. Choose salt-free blends rather than adding salty stock to compensate for less chile heat.

Meal prep: Refrigerate in shallow containers at 40 F or colder within 2 hours, or within 1 hour above 90 F. Store the yogurt separately and use the refrigerated meals and sauce within 3-4 days. Do not repeatedly warm the full batch.

Reheating: Add 1 tablespoon water to one braise/cabbage portion, cover with a vented lid and microwave, stirring between intervals, until the meal reaches 165 F in several places. Alternatively, heat in a covered saucepan, stirring and bringing the braise to a brief boil. Add the cold 70 g yogurt afterward.

Freezing: Freeze hot-component portions that will not be eaten within 3-4 days on prep day. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat the following day. Keep yogurt within its refrigerated window; its texture may separate after freezing.

Portion options: The base makes four substantial meals. For a smaller portion, divide the finished braise and cabbage into five meals and pack about 56 g yogurt per meal. For a larger portion, serve one base meal with 1/2 cup cooked unsalted quinoa (about 90 g); preparing that extra grain is not included in the base recipe time or nutrition.

Health-conscious review: Lean turkey and lentils provide protein, while cabbage, spinach, onion and tomatoes add vegetable volume and fiber. The recipe uses measured olive oil and no-salt-added canned foods. Weight loss or muscle gain depends on total intake and activity, not the recipe title.

Food-safety basis: USDA Leftovers and Food Safety, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/leftovers-and-food-safety. Eating-pattern basis: NIH DASH, https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/dash-eating-plan.
Allergens: Milk; spice blends may contain additional allergens. Original recipe developed for this collection; not kitchen-tested.
